title: Ciambellone
intro: The tall, fluffy Italian breakfast ring cake, scented with lemon.

ing.n: butter and flour for the tin

steps.t: Heat the oven to 175 °C (no fan) and butter and flour a 24 cm ring tin.
Beat eggs and sugar with an electric mixer until pale, thick and holding a ribbon.
steps.label: Whisk

steps.t: Drizzle in the oil and milk, then add the lemon zest and salt, still beating on low speed.
Fold in the sifted flour and baking powder in three goes, lifting from the bottom with a spatula.
Pour into the tin and bake for 45 minutes without opening the oven; a skewer should come out dry.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let the cake rest in the tin, then turn it out onto a wire rack.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Once cool, dust generously with icing sugar.

tips.t: Stir 2 tbsp cocoa into half the batter and layer the two: you get a marbled ciambellone.
Under a cake dome it stays soft for 4 days; from day two it is perfect dunked in milk.

title: Italian apple cake
intro: A soft butter batter packed with apple slices, inside and on top.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 24 cm springform tin with baking paper.
Peel the apples, cut them into thin wedges and toss them with the juice of half the lemon.
Beat eggs and sugar with an electric mixer until pale and foamy.
steps.label: Whisk

steps.t: Add the lukewarm melted butter, milk, lemon zest and salt, then the sifted flour and baking powder.
Dice a third of the apple slices, stir them into the batter and pour it all into the tin.
Arrange the remaining slices in a fan on top, pressing lightly, and sprinkle with brown sugar.
Bake for 45 minutes, until golden on top and a skewer comes out dry.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let the cake cool to lukewarm in the tin before releasing the sides.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Add a teaspoon of cinnamon and a pinch of nutmeg to the batter.
Serve it warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream melting over the apples.

title: Brownies
intro: A shiny crackly top and a fudgy middle: the American chocolate classic.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C and line a 20 cm square tin with baking paper.
Melt chocolate and butter over a pan of simmering water, stirring until glossy, then let it cool slightly.
Whisk eggs, sugar and vanilla for 3 minutes, until foamy.
Stir in the chocolate, then sift in flour, cocoa and salt and mix only until no flour shows.
Add the roughly chopped walnuts and spread the batter evenly in the tin.
Bake for 25 minutes: the edges are set and a skewer in the middle comes out with moist crumbs.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let them cool completely in the tin, then cut into 12 squares.
steps.label: Cool

tips.t: Cut them cold with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry: the squares stay clean.
Swap the walnuts for toasted hazelnuts or a handful of white chocolate chips.
Warm one for 10 seconds and serve it with a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

title: Torta della nonna
intro: Buttery shortcrust, lemon pastry cream and toasted pine nuts on top.

steps.t: Heat the milk with the lemon zest until it steams, without letting it boil.
In a saucepan whisk the yolks with the sugar and cornstarch, then pour in the hot milk slowly, whisking.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the cream thickens and the first bubbles appear.
steps.label: Pastry cream

steps.t: Pour into a bowl, remove the zest, press cling film onto the surface and let it cool.
steps.label: Cool cream

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C. Roll out two thirds of the pastry to 4 mm (chilled ready-made shortcrust works too).
Line a buttered 24 cm tin, prick the base, pour in the cream and cover with the rest of the pastry, sealing the edges.
Brush with a little milk, scatter the pine nuts and bake for 45 minutes, until deep golden.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it cool to lukewarm in the tin, then unmould and dust with icing sugar.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Serve it with a small glass of Tuscan Vin Santo, the way it ends a Sunday lunch in Italy.
Use the cream fully cold: warm cream soaks the pastry and leaves the base underbaked.

title: New York cheesecake
intro: Biscuit base and slow-baked cream cheese filling: dense, smooth, no cracks.

steps.t: Blitz the biscuits, mix with the melted butter and press onto the base of a lined 23 cm springform tin.
Bake the base at 170 °C for 10 minutes, then lower the oven to 150 °C.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Meanwhile beat the room-temperature cream cheese with sugar and flour on low speed until smooth.
Add sour cream, vanilla and zest, then the eggs one at a time, without whipping in too much air.
Pour onto the base and tap the tin gently on the counter to bring bubbles to the surface.
Bake at 150 °C until the edges are set and the centre still wobbles like jelly.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Turn the oven off, prop the door ajar and leave it inside: cooling slowly stops it cracking.
steps.label: Oven off

steps.t: Run a knife around the edge and chill for at least 4 hours before releasing the tin.
steps.label: Chill

tips.t: Serve with a berry sauce: simmer 200 g berries with 40 g sugar for 5 minutes.
Have every ingredient at room temperature so the filling stays smooth and lump-free.
Covered in the fridge it keeps 4 days; it also freezes well in slices.

title: Carrot cake
intro: Moist carrot, walnut and cinnamon cake with cream cheese frosting.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 175 °C, grease and line a 24 cm tin. Finely grate the carrots.
In a bowl mix flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt.
Whisk eggs and brown sugar, then drizzle in the oil until smooth.
Fold in the dry mix, then the carrots and 80 g chopped walnuts, mixing only as much as needed.
Pour into the tin and bake for 50 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it cool completely on a rack: frosting slides off a warm cake.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Meanwhile beat cream cheese, soft butter, icing sugar and vanilla until smooth and firm; keep it in the fridge.
Spread it over the cake with a spatula and finish with the remaining walnuts.

tips.t: Add a teaspoon of ground ginger and the zest of an orange to the batter.
Once frosted, keep it in the fridge and take it out 30 minutes before serving.

title: Torta caprese
intro: Almonds and dark chocolate, no flour: a thin crust and a moist middle.

ing.n: butter and cocoa powder for the tin

steps.t: Heat the oven to 170 °C, butter a 24 cm springform tin and dust it with cocoa.
Pulse the almonds with 2 tbsp of the sugar until finely ground, stopping before they turn to paste.
Melt chocolate and butter over simmering water and let it cool slightly.
Separate the eggs. Whisk the yolks with half the sugar until pale, then stir in chocolate and almonds.
Whisk the whites with the salt and remaining sugar to stiff peaks.
Fold in the whites in three goes, gently lifting from the bottom, and pour into the tin.
Bake for 45 minutes: the top forms a thin crust while the inside stays moist.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it cool in the tin, then unmould and dust with icing sugar.
steps.label: Cool

tips.t: Serve with a spoonful of lightly sweetened whipped cream and a small glass of limoncello.
Toast the almonds at 170 °C for 8 minutes before grinding: the flavour gets much deeper.
White version: use white chocolate, almonds and lemon zest instead of dark chocolate.

title: Vegan chocolate cake
intro: No eggs or butter: vinegar and baking soda make it tall and fluffy.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 180 °C, grease and flour a 22 cm round tin.
In a bowl sift and mix flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt.
In a jug combine water, oil, vinegar and vanilla.
Pour the wet into the dry and whisk only until smooth, then pour into the tin.
Bake for 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out dry.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Turn it out and let it cool on a wire rack.
steps.label: Cool

steps.t: Heat the soy milk, pour it over the chopped chocolate and stir to a glossy glaze.
Pour the glaze over the cold cake, spread it with a spatula and let it set.
steps.label: Glaze

tips.t: Use coffee instead of water: the chocolate flavour gets deeper.
Try a pinch of chilli or cinnamon in the batter.

title: Hotteok, sweet filled pancakes
intro: Chewy yeasted pancakes with a molten centre of brown sugar, cinnamon and walnuts.

steps.t: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the lukewarm water, at about 37 °C.
Add both flours, the salt and 1 tbsp oil and stir to a soft, sticky dough.
Cover and leave to rise somewhere warm until doubled.
steps.label: Rise

steps.t: Meanwhile mix the brown sugar, cinnamon and chopped walnuts: that's the filling.
Oil your hands, divide the dough into 8, flatten each piece in your palm, add a heaped tbsp of filling and pinch tightly closed.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat and add 2 or 3 balls, seam side down, until golden underneath.
steps.label: First side

steps.t: Flip and press flat with an oiled spatula to 1 cm thick; lower the heat, cover and cook until the filling melts.
steps.label: Press

steps.t: Flip once more for 30 seconds and serve hot; wait a minute before biting in, the melted sugar is scalding.

tips.t: Oil your hands well: the dough is meant to be sticky, that's what makes it chewy.
Add sunflower and pumpkin seeds to the filling for Busan-style ssiat hotteok.

title: Pistachio baklava
intro: Layers of buttery filo and pistachio soaked in syrup: crisp on top, soft underneath.

steps.t: For the syrup, bring the sugar and water to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the lemon juice and let it cool completely.
steps.label: Syrup

steps.t: Meanwhile melt the butter over low heat, skim the foam and pour off only the clear part, leaving the milky solids behind.
Coarsely chop the pistachios; keep 2 tbsp finely ground for decoration. Heat the oven to 180 °C.
Butter a 30x20 cm tin. Trim the filo to fit and keep it covered with a damp tea towel.
Lay down half the sheets one at a time, brushing each with butter.
Spread over the pistachios, then cover with the remaining sheets, buttering each; be generous on the top one.
With a sharp knife, cut into diamonds or squares right down to the bottom before baking.
Bake for 50 minutes, until deep golden and crisp; if it browns too soon, lower to 170 °C.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: As soon as it comes out, pour the cold syrup all over the hot baklava: it should sizzle.
Leave uncovered for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, out of the fridge. Sprinkle with the ground pistachio.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Cold syrup on hot baklava (or the reverse, never both hot): that's how it stays crisp.
At Turkish shops look for baklava yufka, thinner than filo: more layers, more crunch.
Keeps 1 week at room temperature under a sheet of paper: never in the fridge.

title: Galaktoboureko (custard filo pie)
intro: Milk and semolina custard between buttery filo layers, soaked in lemon syrup.

steps.t: For the syrup, boil the water, 250 g sugar, a strip of lemon peel and the cinnamon; then let it cool completely.
steps.label: Syrup

steps.t: Heat the milk with half the custard sugar, rain in the semolina while whisking and cook on low until thick.
steps.label: Custard

steps.t: Off the heat stir in 40 g butter, vanilla and grated lemon zest; beat the eggs with the remaining sugar and whisk them in.
Butter a 22 x 30 cm dish and lay in half the filo, one sheet at a time, brushing each with melted butter.
Pour in the custard, fold over the edges and cover with the remaining buttered filo; score diamonds in the top layers only.
Bake at 180 °C until the top is deep golden and crisp.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Slowly pour the cold syrup over the hot pie and let it soak in; cut only once it is lukewarm.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Cold syrup on a hot pie: that way the filo soaks it up without going soggy.
Keeps covered in the fridge for 3 days; take it out half an hour before serving.

title: Pear and almond tart (Bourdaloue)
intro: Poached pears on almond cream in a sweet crust: a Paris pâtisserie classic.

ing.n: ripe but firm pears (Williams or Bartlett)
f: ripe but firm pear (Williams or Bartlett)
ripe but firm pears (Williams or Bartlett)

steps.t: Bring the water, 100 g sugar and the lemon juice to a boil; poach the peeled, halved and cored pears until tender.
steps.label: Pears

steps.t: Turn off the heat and let the pears cool in the syrup.
steps.label: Cooling

steps.t: Meanwhile heat the oven to 180 °C, line a 24 cm tart tin with the pastry (shop-bought is fine), prick it and chill.
Beat the soft butter with 100 g sugar, then add the eggs one at a time, the ground almonds, flour and vanilla.
Spread the almond cream over the pastry. Drain and dry the pears, slice them thinly and fan them out, pressing lightly.
Scatter with flaked almonds and bake on the lower shelf until the almond cream is puffed and golden.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let the tart cool in its tin until just warm.
steps.label: Cooling

steps.t: Warm the jam with a spoonful of water and brush it over the pears to glaze. Serve warm or at room temperature.

tips.t: Canned pear halves in syrup let you skip the poaching and save half an hour.
Serve with a spoonful of crème fraîche or softly whipped cream.
It keeps for 2 days covered at room temperature; the almond cream stays moist.
